name: Morva Black Sesame-Cardamom Praline
description: Individual praline rounds made with a black sesame paste center, cardamom-infused synth-cocoa shell, and a thin gold-luster finish. Sold in boxes of six, each praline in a paper cup. Morva's black sesame-cardamom variant is their second-best seller after the Deep Cocoa line, prized for its complexity.
flavor_profile: Immediate cardamom warmth from the shell, yielding to dense roasted black sesame paste — rich, slightly bitter, nutty — with a synth-cocoa finish that lingers; the gold luster is flavorless but contributes to the ritual of eating it
cultural_context: Morva pralines are a gift item first, a personal indulgence second. They appear at Tier 3-4 business meetings, romantic occasions, and condolence gestures. The box design is understated enough to avoid looking ostentatious while signaling genuine expenditure. In Tier 5, they're considered quaint but acceptable to give to staff. The pralines contain no real cocoa — Morva has never claimed otherwise — but they're engineered well enough that most consumers don't raise the point.
story_hooks: A Morva praline box delivered to a Tier 4 executive contained a praline with a different weight — inside the shell, replacing the sesame paste, is a data bead.
Morva is quietly sourcing one ingredient from a the Gray Zone-level synth-farm under a shell company; the origin would destroy their luxury positioning if revealed.
A Tier 5 Spire resident has been sending Morva boxes to the same Tier 2 address every month for three years — no card, no return label, and the recipient has no idea who sends them.
related_entities: ARCTURUS DEFENSE Bastion Subdermal Armor Mesh
